problem: Whether to acquire a small online rental competitor.
title: Blockbuster declines an offer to buy Netflix
context: In early 2000 Netflix was a small, money-losing DVD-by-mail company and Blockbuster was far larger.
decision_made: Decline Netflix's reported offer to sell for $50 million.
action_taken: Ended the talks; Blockbuster's CEO regarded Netflix as a very small niche business.
observed_outcome: Netflix's CEO later said he was grateful Blockbuster had not bought it. The sources used do not cover Blockbuster's later results.
lessons: A small competitor with a different model can be dismissed because of its current size rather than its direction.
limitations: Blockbuster's CEO disputes that serious talks took place. Accounts come mostly from Netflix founders. Later outcomes for Blockbuster were not checked here.

claims.claim_text: Netflix's founders offered to sell to Blockbuster for $50 million and Blockbuster declined.
Netflix's CEO said he was grateful Blockbuster did not want to buy it.
